Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Mikko Saari wrote:
> Does Dodge help even though [Muddled Vampire Hunter] hits with First Strike?

6.4.5. Strike Effects

Dodge. A Dodge strike deals no damage, but it protects the dodging minion
and his possessions from the effects of the opposing strike. Retainers are
not protected, however. A Dodge is effective at any range.

Messages.Author: David Bowsky
Messages.Body:
I thought the whole "First Strike" thing canceled out the dodge (unless
the vamp somehow has a 'Dodge with First Strike' which seems kinda
silly.)

We always figured if a 'First Strike' sends someone to torpor (ie.
Sengier.. Ivory Bow, etc) that the torp'd vamp has no opportunity for a
return strike.

Similarly, that considering the FS, the dodge would occur when the
vamp's strike would normally occur, ie after the FS had been assessed.

Was this an errata or were we always wrong? :)

>
> Similarly, that considering the FS, the dodge would occur when the
> vamp's strike would normally occur, ie after the FS had been assessed.
>
> Was this an errata or were we always wrong? :)

It has always been this way, although the Jyhad rules could be read either
way:

Jyhad: "Dodge: The Dodge strike card deals no damage, but it negates the effect
of the opponent's strike that round." [15.3] (note: no limitation of "unless
the strike was done with first strike").

To clear up the ambiguity, the Rules Team issued the following Ruling:
"Dodge will cancel a first strike." [RTR 22-DEC-1994]

V:TES: "Dodge: A "dodge" deals no damage, but it prevents the effect of the
opponent's strike that round, even if the opponent's strike was delivered
with First Strike." [8.3]
